solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One's point of view, in the main

definitions.text: One's point of view, in the main

parts.words: One's point of view, in the main
parts.note: the main is the sea, and a ship's round window is where a sailor looks out on it

explanation.surface: Someone states their opinion, which mostly runs a certain way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the main' looks like 'mostly', but here it means 'on the open sea', so the viewpoint is a literal window on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's small round window is literally where a sailor gets a view while at sea.

clue.text: Figure worktop had been removed ages after

indicators.note: places the word for ages behind the shortened word for work
says the top letter of the work word is taken away, leaving the rest

parts.note: read as work plus top: work is a job, and its top letter is the one that goes
for ages means for a long time

explanation.surface: Someone's kitchen counter was taken out a long while back.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'worktop' has to be read as two words, 'work top', so 'top had been removed' acts on the word for work; 'after' places the ages word last.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectangle longer than it is wide is a geometrical figure of this shape.

clue.text: Chucked over, it is said

indicators.note: signals that a word is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: something over is finished, through

explanation.surface: Someone reports that a ball was tossed across, or a match was abandoned.
explanation.definitionFit: Chucked is a casual synonym of tossed or flung, past tense to match.

clue.text: So then going to pieces when one is about to win

definitions.note: in betting, a stake only on first place

indicators.note: the word one surrounds the other letters

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: falling apart, so the letters of so then are rearranged

explanation.surface: A punter collapses just as their horse is about to triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going to pieces' is the anagram signal and 'is about' the container. The definition is the racing sense: a bet placed only on the horse winning, not on a place.
explanation.definitionFit: A bet placed this way pays only if the horse wins outright, not for a place.

clue.text: Great exit. I leave again by myself

indicators.note: the letter I departs from the word before it

parts.note: taken as written
re- is a prefix meaning again
me is the speaker's word for themselves

explanation.surface: A dramatic departure: the speaker walks out once more, alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I leave' takes the I out of EXIT to give EXT; 'by' merely joins ME on.
explanation.definitionFit: Great in the sense of very intense or utmost, as in great or severe danger.

clue.text: Cap for racegoer

definitions.meaning: to cap something is to top or outdo it
someone at the races who places wagers

explanation.surface: A hat suitable for a day at the races.
explanation.definitionFit: To cap is to surpass, and a punter at the course is one who wagers.

clue.text: Created only to accommodate superstar cast do

indicators.note: the word for only takes the other letters in

parts.note: but means only, as in 'but a child'

indicators.note: cast off, thrown away, so the following letters go

parts.note: an idol is a hugely admired star
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something made solely to house a celebrity's party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast do' looks like a party for the cast, but 'cast' means thrown off, removing the letters of 'do' from the superstar word; 'to accommodate' is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Something built has been constructed or made, so created fits as a past participle.

clue.text: Withdraws attempts to get refund

definitions.meaning: returns goods to a shop for one's money

explanation.surface: Someone pulls out of trying to recover their money.
explanation.definitionFit: One retracts a statement this way, and a shopper returns an item to the store for money.

clue.text: Coming in to hypnotise

definitions.meaning: an arrival or way into a place
to put into a trance, or to enchant

explanation.surface: Arriving in order to mesmerise someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun for an arrival and a verb meaning put under a spell share this spelling.

clue.text: Carrying large crate out — wine

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold the abbreviation inside them
crate is out of order, so its letters are shuffled

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Someone lugs a big box out of the cellar: it holds wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges CRATE to CARET, and 'Carrying' has it hold L.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is the British name for red Bordeaux, a kind of wine.

clue.text: They're woods, stupid! Mixed set

parts.note: thick is informal for dim or stupid

indicators.note: the letters of set are jumbled up

explanation.surface: An exasperated golfer: those are woods, idiot, a mixed set of clubs!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixed' rearranges SET to ETS. 'Woods' and 'set' suggest golf clubs, but the woods are dense clusters of trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Dense growths of shrubs and trees are small woods, plural to match 'They're'.

clue.text: Year when all goes wrong, regardless of location

indicators.note: everything is disordered, so the letters of year when are scrambled

explanation.surface: A bad year when everything fails, wherever you are.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something happens in any place at all means place makes no difference.

clue.text: In Italy, you study Italian

parts.note: tu is the Italian familiar word for you
to scan is to examine closely

explanation.surface: In Italy, you learn the language.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuscany is a region of Italy, so a native of it is Italian.

clue.text: In which one parades one's grievances?

definitions.text: In which one parades one's grievances?

parts.words: In which one parades one's grievances?
parts.note: parades is literal: complaints carried through the streets on banners

explanation.surface: A question about the occasion when someone shows off their complaints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parades' looks figurative, meaning showing off, but here the grievances are literally carried in procession.
explanation.definitionFit: A demonstration where people walk the streets carrying slogans about their complaints.

clue.text: Favoured, before fellow slipped up

parts.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before
erred means made a mistake

explanation.surface: The favourite, once the man made a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: Something chosen over others is liked better, the same past-tense sense.

clue.text: Zodiacal sign he's found in a reference book

indicators.note: the letters of he's are placed within the star sign

parts.note: Taurus, the bull, is a sign of the zodiac
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A man is a Taurus, according to a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' is the container signal; 'he's' keeps its letters but drops the apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: A book of words grouped with their synonyms is a work of reference.

clue.text: Lacking the energy to bend over?

definitions.text: Lacking the energy to bend over?

parts.words: Lacking the energy to bend over?
parts.note: to list is to lean or bend over, so without lists means without leaning

explanation.surface: Too tired even to stoop down.
explanation.walkthrough: A ship lists when it leans; something with no such lean is, punningly, without a list.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethargic or lacking vigour, the everyday meaning, with a second reading as 'not leaning'.

clue.text: As the snooker player said to Lady Luck?

definitions.text: As the snooker player said to Lady Luck?

parts.words: As the snooker player said to Lady Luck?
parts.note: a snooker player opening the frame wants a good break, and the cry also means 'let up on me'

explanation.surface: A snooker player pleading with fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: The break in snooker is the opening shot or a run of scoring; the phrase is also an everyday plea for leniency.
explanation.definitionFit: An exasperated plea to stop being so harsh, here also a request for a good opening shot.

clue.text: They support those who are in retreat

definitions.meaning: people who fund or champion a cause

explanation.surface: Supporters are the ones falling back.
explanation.definitionFit: Sponsors who fund something, and also, punningly, people moving backwards.

clue.text: Charged for bunk I shall occupy

indicators.note: the letters for I shall take up the space inside the bed

parts.note: a bunk is a bed
I'll is the contraction of I shall, written without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone is charged for a bunk they will sleep in.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sent an invoice means being charged, past tense matching.

clue.text: Rest, unwinding before morning rush

indicators.note: untwisting, so the letters of rest are reordered

parts.note: a.m. abbreviates the Latin for before noon, morning

explanation.surface: Relaxing before the morning commute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unwinding' looks like relaxing, the surface sense of rest, but it signals that the letters of 'Rest' are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A rush of water, or a stream of people pouring along, is a flow.

clue.text: Gets hitched and loves showing the wife round

indicators.note: the title goes round the zeros

parts.note: Mrs is the title of a married woman
love is zero in tennis, written as the letter O, so two of them

explanation.surface: A newly-wed adores the wife who shows them around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets hitched' suggests marrying, but a boat is hitched, or tied up, at a quay.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat is tied up to a fixed point, which is to be hitched or made fast.

clue.text: He looks good in uniform

parts.note: a clergyman serving the armed forces looks to the good of those in uniform

explanation.surface: A man is handsome in his dress uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looks good' seems to praise his appearance; read it as 'looks after the good' of the troops.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman attached to a regiment cares for the spiritual welfare of soldiers.

clue.text: Be stuck in a home

definitions.meaning: become firmly fixed, as a bone in the throat
a small house, such as a gatekeeper's cottage

explanation.surface: Being trapped in a house.
explanation.definitionFit: Something becomes jammed in place this way, and the noun is a cottage or dwelling.

clue.text: Rough sea for yours truly is terrifying

indicators.note: rough as of a sea, so the letters of sea for are churned

parts.note: a jocular way for the speaker to mean themselves, me

explanation.surface: A choppy sea is frightening for the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Frightening or alarming, the same adjective sense.

clue.text: Sift through possible material for a children's book

definitions.meaning: to pass through a coarse sieve

definitions.text: possible material for a children's book
definitions.meaning: a puzzle question of the sort printed in children's joke books

explanation.surface: Someone combs through potential content for a picture book.
explanation.definitionFit: A coarse sieve, used as a verb, and a puzzling question found in joke books for children.

clue.text: Whispers 'Team's ahead'

parts.note: read as 'a head': the letter A placed at the head
a side is a team, so team's is side's, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone murmurs that their team is in the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ahead' is split as 'a head', putting A at the front. On stage, an actor's remark the other characters supposedly cannot hear.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatrical remarks spoken to the audience, like murmurs not meant for others onstage.

clue.text: Puts off giving passes to let us in

indicators.note: let ... in admits something, here the word us inside
with let, says the word us goes within the other

parts.note: one passes or spends time
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone postpones issuing entry passes for the group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let ... in' is the container signal, split around 'us'; 'passes' is the verb, as one passes or spends time.
explanation.definitionFit: To postpone or defer a decision is to hold it in abeyance, present tense matching.
